narrative:
The model predicts you have a 31% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your past academic record, your ambitions for higher education, and your mother's occupation. Surprisingly, the strongest influence came from your number of past class failures. Even though you have had zero failures so far, this absence of prior failure actually pushed the model toward expecting you to pass, not fail. The second most important factor was your clear desire to pursue higher education. This strongly pulled the prediction in a positive direction because every student who passed also expressed the same goal. The third key influence was your mother's job in the services sector. This characteristic slightly increased the chance the model gave for failing, as it is less commonly seen among students who ultimately passed.

Although the overall risk is moderate, these elements together tipped the balance enough to trigger the remedial requirement. To improve your chances, focus on maintaining the strong motivation you already have for higher education and consider adding consistent weekly study time, since only about one in five students who passed studied less than two hours per week. Building steady study habits now can help turn your 31% risk into a much safer outcome. (218 words)
